title: Human Rights, Democracy and Discrimination
summary: The Bill of Rights and the limitation of rights, discrimination and human rights violations, the role of institutions such as the SAHRC and Constitutional Court, and how citizens participate in democracy.

notes.text: Chapter 2 of the Constitution (1996), the **Bill of Rights**, protects the rights of everyone in South Africa. It is based on **human dignity, equality and freedom**.

Rights are not absolute. **Section 36** allows rights to be limited by law if the limitation is **reasonable and justifiable** in an open and democratic society. For example, freedom of expression does not protect **hate speech** or incitement to violence, and freedom of movement can be limited by a court order.

rows: Refusing service to someone because of race
Paying women less for the same work; domestic abuse
Attacks on foreign nationals and their shops
Bullying or attacking someone because of sexual orientation
Buildings without access for wheelchair users

notes.label: Fair or unfair?
notes.text: Section 9 forbids **unfair** discrimination. Some measures that treat groups differently (affirmative action, ramps for wheelchair users, bursaries for poor students) are allowed because they **advance equality**.

rows: Promotes and protects human rights; investigates complaints
Investigates abuse of power and maladministration in government
Checks how public money is spent

notes.text: The **Constitutional Court** is the highest court on constitutional matters and can declare laws or government actions invalid.

items: Join the Representative Council of Learners (RCL), youth organisations and community forums.
Sign petitions, write to representatives, take part in peaceful protest.
Report human rights violations to the SAHRC, police or Childline.

questions.prompt: Which section of the Constitution allows rights to be limited?

Which institution investigates abuse of power by government officials?
Match each institution to its role.
Explain why building ramps for wheelchair users is not unfair discrimination.

✓ It treats a group differently in order to give them equal access (1)
